offlineProtection.explainerLead: During service your dashboard or kitchen display (KDS) must stay on and connected to the internet.
offlineProtection.explainerBody: If the screen turns off, the device loses internet, or you switch to another website, offline protection takes over — depending on what you chose, it pauses ordering or turns auto-accept off.
offlineProtection.reminder: ⚠️ During service keep your dashboard or kitchen display (KDS) on and connected to the internet; otherwise offline protection may take over.
offlineProtection.enableConfirm:
Offline protection is on.

For orders to keep coming in without interruption, your screen must stay on. If this device loses its connection, offline protection takes over in the mode you chose.

Make sure “Keep screen on” is switched on on this device.
offlineProtection.disableConfirm:
Turn off offline protection for this event?

If this device loses its connection, online orders will continue — customers may place orders you can’t see. Only turn it off if you have a reliable connection.
offlineProtection.cardDescription: Decides what happens to incoming orders when your device is offline.
offlineProtection.purpose: If your device loses its connection, this stops orders coming in while you can’t see them.
offlineProtection.switchHelp: What happens when this vehicle loses its connection.
offlineProtection.modes.pause.label: Pause taking online orders
offlineProtection.modes.pause.help: Customers can’t order until you are online again.
offlineProtection.modes.no_auto_accept.l: Keep taking orders, confirm them yourself
offlineProtection.modes.no_auto_accept.h: Auto-accept is turned off, so customers can still order but nothing is confirmed automatically. When you are online again you confirm each one — any order still waiting is rejected automatically after the time you chose, and the customer is told by email.
offlineProtection.autoRejectLabel: Reject orders that have waited longer than:
kitchenCapacity.desc: The maximum number of items your kitchen can turn out at once across all the categories you ticked. Each category’s own batch size also applies on top.
kitchenCapacity.example: Example: if you can cook 4 main dishes in 5 minutes, set 4 items every 5 minutes. The total capacity limits orders across all selected categories; so if you only want to sell at most 10 starters and mains every 5 minutes, set Total capacity to 10 items every 5 minutes and tick the Starters and Mains boxes. Even so, your mains stay at only 4 items every 5 minutes.
kitchenCapacity.noLimit: Leave it on the infinity symbol (∞) for no limit.
kitchenCapacity.warning: ⚠️ For kitchen capacity to work properly, set a prep time and batch size on your menu categories (Menu & Stock). Without them, capacity can’t know how long items take to cook.
kitchenCapacity.noVan: Add a vehicle in Settings › Vehicle settings to set your kitchen capacity.
kitchenCapacity.lead: How many items your kitchen can prepare, so customers only choose collection times you can meet.
kitchenCapacity.sameForAll: Same kitchen capacity for all vehicles?
kitchenCapacity.confirmBody: All vehicles will use this vehicle’s kitchen capacity: {van}. Each vehicle’s own figures will be replaced.
kitchenCapacity.colCountsTitle: Which categories count in the total capacity. Cooked categories always count; tick the instant ones (sides, sauces, drinks) to include them.
kitchenCapacity.countsLocked: Cooked — always counts (its prep time and batch set the pace)
kitchenCapacity.countsNoCap: Set a capacity to choose which categories count
kitchenCapacity.countsUnavailable: Unavailable until the database is updated
kitchenCapacity.countsTick: Tick to include this instant category (sides, sauces, drinks) in the shared time-window limit
kitchenCapacity.setCapacityFirst: Set a capacity to choose which categories count.

kitchenCapacity.categoryPrepAria: {hasCategory, select, yes {{category} — prep time} other {prep time}}
kitchenCapacity.prepPerOrderHelp: How long one order takes to prepare
kitchenCapacity.itemsAtATimeHelp: How many items your kitchen can cook at once
kitchenCapacity.instantNote: Instant items don’t count in kitchen capacity — customers receive them immediately.
settingsCopy.allowCancellation.label: Allow customers to cancel orders
settingsCopy.allowCancellation.sentence: Customers can cancel up to <select></select> before the collection time arrives
settingsCopy.autoAccept.label: Accept orders automatically
settingsCopy.autoAccept.help: Orders are confirmed automatically. If the requested slot is full, the order moves to the next open slot. It only confirms when there is capacity. Orders with a customer note (e.g. an allergy) still have to be confirmed by you.
settingsCopy.orderReady.label: Order-ready step
settingsCopy.orderReady.help: Shows a “Mark ready” button on the orders page. The kitchen display (KDS) is set separately on each device. Customers get an email every time an order is marked ready. Applies to all events — but for one event you can turn it on or off on its dashboard.
settingsCopy.buzzers.label: Do you give out buzzers for collection?
settingsCopy.buzzers.help: Record which buzzer you gave each customer, so you know who to look for when their food is ready.
settingsCopy.buzzers.countLabel: How many buzzers do you have?
whereYouTrade.stepHeading: Where is your food truck based?
whereYouTrade.stepIntro: This decides your currency, prices, time zone and phone number format. The country can’t be changed later because it is tied to your card payments.
whereYouTrade.countryGuessed: We guessed this from where you are. Change it if it isn’t right.
whereYouTrade.townQuestion: The town/city you are based in
whereYouTrade.saveFailed: Couldn’t save the settings — please try again.
stockCopy.defaultScopeNote: It is the default for all events. To set a different amount for one event, change it on that event’s dashboard — events you already set there keep their own amount.
managePrimitives.allergenMode.perDishBod: Review each dish and confirm its allergens. Customers see each dish’s markers and an allergen summary card made from them.
managePrimitives.allergenMode.cardBody: Upload or paste one allergen card (PDF, image or text); it is shown as it is. Each dish’s markers stay hidden.
manageSettings.walkthrough.title: Is HatchGrab new to you?
manageSettings.walkthrough.body: A short tour showing what is on each tab. Takes about a minute.
manageSettings.getApp.title: Download the app
manageSettings.getApp.body: The kitchen app runs your service on a phone or tablet — and it is also the only way to keep taking orders when the network drops. Comes free with your account; for iPhone, iPad and Android.
manageSettings.logo.label: Logo
manageSettings.logo.removeConfirm: Remove your logo? Customers will see your food truck’s name without a logo. You can upload a new logo at any time.
manageSettings.logo.removeFailed: Couldn’t remove the logo — please try again.

manageSettings.contact.emailHelp: The address where you receive new-order notifications — also shown on customers’ confirmation when the contact method chosen below is “Email”.

manageSettings.schedule.title: Your schedule
manageSettings.schedule.autoDesc: Tell us where you post your schedule; we will check it for you and send the events we find for you to approve. This must be your own website — not a Facebook or Instagram page.
manageSettings.schedule.eitherWay: Either way, if we find your events listed somewhere else, we will still send them for you to approve. Nothing goes live until you confirm it.
manageSettings.schedule.wherePost: Where do you post your schedule?
manageSettings.schedule.checkingHelp: This can take up to 2 minutes — please keep this page open and don’t close the tab.
manageSettings.schedule.urlHelp: Your website where customers see your upcoming events — not a Facebook or Instagram page
manageSettings.schedule.exclusionsHelp: These words are filtered out automatically when you import your schedule. Remove any that were added by mistake.
manageSettings.qr.title: Order QR code
manageSettings.qr.domainLive: This QR code now sends customers here: <mono>{domain}</mono>. You never need to print a new one.
manageSettings.qr.domainNotLive: This QR code sends customers to your HatchGrab ordering page. If you later set up your own web address, the same QR code will send them there instead — you won’t need to print a new one.
manageSettings.qr.printHelp: Print or display this code so customers can scan it and place a pre-order. Put it at the truck or on your vehicle, or share it online.
manageSettings.qr.noUrl: No order link yet — your food truck’s page address hasn’t been set.

manageSettings.qr.lockedTitle: Codes with a logo are switched off for your food truck
manageSettings.qr.lockedBody: Codes with a logo are switched off for your food truck. Your standard QR code works exactly the same for customers — the only difference is your logo in the middle.
manageSettings.qr.buildFailed: That couldn’t be made right now. Wait a little and try again.

manageReports.accounts.title: For your accountant
manageReports.accounts.help: Sales are counted on the event day. Gross means what customers paid. Net means what is left after refunds and tax are taken off.
manageReports.accounts.taxNone: No tax rate is set for your food truck, so no tax is calculated here.

manageReports.accounts.eventNoProfit: A dash (—) means not all dishes sold there have a cost.
manageReports.accounts.downloadHelp: Two spreadsheet files: one with a row for each order, the other with a row for each event. They open in Excel, Numbers, Xero and QuickBooks.
